note: 35 practitioner interviews and 435 tools reviewed, the best available map of where audit tooling actually falls short.
title: Towards AI Accountability Infrastructure: Gaps and Opportunities in AI Audit Tooling
journal: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
explain_beginner: This research examines tools that organizations use to check if artificial intelligence systems are working safely and fairly. Researchers interviewed 35 people who conduct these audits and reviewed 435 different tools. They found that while many tools exist to measure AI performance, they struggle to support real accountability. The study identifies gaps in current tools and calls for developing better infrastructure that helps practitioners not just evaluate AI, but also discover problems and advocate for fixes.
explain_business: Organizations deploying AI systems lack adequate tooling to fully audit their systems for risks and accountability. This research maps available solutions against practitioner needs and reveals significant shortfalls, particularly in identifying harms and supporting accountability mechanisms. Decision-makers should understand that current evaluation tools alone are insufficient for responsible AI deployment. The findings suggest opportunities for tool developers to address unmet needs in comprehensive audit infrastructure, and they indicate that organizations may need multiple solutions to meet accountability requirements.
explain_practitioner: This paper presents findings from 35 practitioner interviews and analysis of 435 audit tools to map the AI audit tooling ecosystem against actual needs. Results show that current tools primarily focus on evaluation and standard-setting but inadequately support accountability functions. Key gaps include insufficient support for harms discovery and advocacy work. The authors argue that the field requires moving beyond evaluation-centric tooling toward comprehensive accountability infrastructure that addresses the full scope of audit practitioner workflows.
